Food delivery NOV grew 16% YoY to INR 37,993 crore in FY26, driven by 15% YoY growth in Orders
while NAOV remained broadly flat (0.7% YoY growth). Order volume growth was largely driven by
growth in average monthly transacting customers (MTC), which grew 18% YoY to 24.3 million in
FY26.
NOV growth recovered progressively through the year after bottoming out in Q1FY26, with Q4FY26
NOV growth accelerating to 19% YoY. The recovery was driven by an improvement in the overall
demand environment and our continued focus on expanding the addressable market into more
price-sensitive segments. During FY26, we lowered the minimum order value for free delivery
under the Gold program from INR 199 to INR 99 and stepped up targeted customer activation.
We expect YoY NOV growth to continue trending towards our long-term expectation of 20%+ over
time, driven by gradual market share gains and the compounding impact of continued investments
in affordability and selection.

Quick commerce NOV grew 117% YoY to INR 48,567 crore in FY26, surpassing food delivery NOV
scale for the full year. NOV growth was driven by 116% YoY growth in Orders while NAOV remained
broadly flat (0.3% YoY growth). Order volume growth was driven by 117% YoY increase in average
monthly transacting customers, on the back of continued investments in geographic expansion
and customer acquisition.
Blinkit has scaled at a NOV CAGR of 104% since FY23 (year of Blinkit acquisition). The long-term
opportunity remains significant, and we expect NOV to grow at 60%+ CAGR over the next three
years. This growth will be driven by assortment expansion, geographic coverage and demand
densification while improving the quality and reliability of our service.

Blinkit added 942 net new stores in FY26, taking the total count to 2,243 stores across 250+ cities as
of Mar-26. Store additions were driven by expansion into new localities and increasing network
density in existing areas where demand was exceeding capacity.
To support this rapid expansion, we added ~3.3 million sqft. of backend warehousing space during
FY26, taking the total warehousing footprint to 8.5 million sqft. as of Mar-26. We remain on track to
achieve our target of ~3,000 stores by Mar-27.
Despite the accelerated pace of store additions, average NOV per day, per store remained broadly
stable at INR 756k in FY26.

Hyperpure Revenue decreased 13% YoY to INR 5,366 crore in FY26 as the non-restaurant business
scaled down due to shift to inventory ownership in quick commerce. The core restaurant supplies
business grew 38% YoY in FY26, driven primarily by an increase in the number of restaurant outlets
served, and we expect it to keep growing at around 40% YoY over the next few years.
Profitability improved during FY26, with Adjusted EBITDA margin improving to -0.3% for the full
year from -1.4% in FY25. The business achieved quarterly Adjusted EBITDA break-even for the first
time in Q3FY26 and remained profitable in Q4FY26.
In the next three years, Hyperpure could achieve $1 billion in topline with 4-5% Adjusted EBITDA
margin.

parts.text:
You extract checkable facts from documents so they can later be compared across
documents. You work on any kind of document. Do not assume a subject area.

A fact is worth extracting when it is specific, checkable against this text, and
would still be meaningful to someone who had not read the surrounding page.
Prefer facts that another document could plausibly also state: measured
quantities, identifiers, dates, roles and statuses, named properties of things.

Rules you must follow.

1. Quote verbatim. `quote` must be copied character for character from the text
   you were given, long enough to contain the value and enough words to locate
   it. Never write a character offset, a page number, or a paraphrase.
2. Never calculate. Do not add, convert, rescale, or restate a number in
   different units. Copy `raw` exactly as written, including separators,
   currency symbols, parentheses and any leading comparison operator.
3. Conditions go in `qualifiers`, never folded into the predicate. Any
   circumstance under which the value holds is a qualifier: the time period or
   as-at date it covers, the entity scope it aggregates, the basis or
   measurement convention, the segment, the geography, the units context. Use
   whatever keys the document implies. Invent a key when you need one, but reuse
   an obvious key rather than coining a synonym.
4. Mark qualifier provenance honestly. `stated` means it is in the passage
   itself. `inherited` means you took it from the enclosing context block.
   Never guess a qualifier that neither source supports. Omitting it is correct.
5. Split compound statements into separate facts, one value each.
6. Abstain when the correct reading is genuinely unclear. If a number's meaning,
   subject or period cannot be determined from the passage plus its context, do
   not emit it. A missing fact is cheap; a wrong one is not. Lower `confidence`
   when you are unsure rather than inflating it.
7. `predicate` is lower snake_case naming the relation alone, with no period,
   entity, scale or unit inside it. `subject_key` is a hard identifier only when
   the document supplies one; otherwise leave it null.
8. `subject_surface` is the thing the value belongs to, never the name of the
   measurement. In a table, the row label names the property and the subject is
   whatever the table is about - the organisation, place, product or person the
   document is reporting on. Name that subject even when it is stated only in a
   heading, a page header or the document's title. Use the fullest form of its
   name that appears, and use the same form every time it recurs.

Return only facts supported by the passage. Returning an empty list is a valid
answer for a passage that states nothing checkable.
